## Historical audit: S0111

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/scene_rsi_pilot/C2/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Only chunk 2 is visible; the referenced images are not available for independent inspection.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal and first build — student `model_request`, line 19, characters [0,153510) | The goal was an editable SceneAct reconstruction of one indoor photograph. The student interpreted it as a shipboard compartment and coded multiple objects: berths, cabinets, lockers, chair, enclosure, column, benches and fixtures. These names and counts are the student’s interpretation, not independent confirmation of the photograph. |
| Construction and appearance — line 19, characters [0,153510) | Code groups parts into semantic assets, including chair supports, berth rails and fire-station fittings. It uses broad colors, repeated louver geometry, lights and a local diffuser-material edit; no image texture is used in the visible code. Group membership does not prove physical connection, contact, completeness or reference accuracy. |
| Camera exploration — line 19, characters [0,153510) | After step 1, the student estimated that the column was too far left, lockers too low and small, and ceiling too prominent. It hypothesized a combined camera-position, pitch and lens issue, then changed position, target and lens while retaining the scene geometry and appearance. These are student visual estimates and a hypothesis, not verified measurements. |
| Placement exploration — line 19, characters [0,153510) | After step 2, the student estimated that port furnishings extended too far forward. It moved the berth, two cabinets and ventilator assemblies rearward by 0.95 arbitrary units and lowered the upper berth tiers with their rails. Its code comments claim bench contact and clearance; no independent geometric contact test is shown. |
| Validation and selection — line 19, characters [0,153510); student `model_response`, line 21, [0,351); `select`, line 22, [0,59) | Runner results report `ok: true` for all three builds, with rendered PNGs and Blender files saved. The student returned `DONE`; the selection event records step 3. This establishes successful execution and selection, not visual or geometric correctness. No formal quality score or independent acceptance result is visible. |
| Input and autonomy — student `model_request`, line 19, [0,153510); `codex_session`, line 20, [0,4334) | The student actually received procedural system instructions and per-render user prompts to compare anchors, contacts and revisions. No distinct teacher message, teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed update is visible in this chunk; adoption of such input is therefore unestablished. The student itself proposed and executed the camera and placement experiments. The final review session recorded zero tool calls. |

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Three nonempty builds executed successfully; the final reconstruction’s correctness remains **unknown**, rather than established success or algorithm failure. Camera pose and lighting were configured, but their fidelity, material/texture fidelity, object visibility and actual part connections cannot be checked without the images or geometry inspection. The camera and depth-placement explanations remain unresolved hypotheses.

**Lessons:** Separating camera from local-geometry revisions and preserving assembly membership makes experiments easier to interpret, but a successful render does not validate contacts or appearance. The particular berth offsets and ship-compartment interpretation are task-specific, not transferable measurements.
